To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the endogenous labor supply and the services derived from the public capital can generate complex dynamic behavior.
the endogenous labor-supply and public-capital models are capable of producing multiple balanced-growth equilibria, limit cycles, and local and global indetermination.

in a model where the services derived from capital are congested by households but not by units of time, a large lump-sum subsidy to the capital accumulation process is necessary for the occurrence of local and global indeterminate equilibria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of fiscal policy on the dynamic equilibrium of a small open economy with endogenous growth.
the role of the government in the process of economic growth and the effects of fiscal policy on economic growth.
the effects of public capital and fiscal policy on the long-run growth of a small open economy with an endogenous labor supply.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of public capital and a large lump-sum taxation are necessary conditions for obtaining a complex dynamic equilibrium behavior in the endogenous-growth framework.

the introduction of public capital and endogenous labor supply in an endogenous growth model can lead to complex dynamic behavior, which is not possible when only private capital is present in the economy.
the introduction of public capital in the model is a necessary and sufficient condition for the occurrence of complex dynamics in the endogenous-growth models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endogenous labor supply is a necessary ingredient to obtain complex dynamics in endogenous-growth models with public capital.
the existence of multiple balanced-growth equilibria is not a sufficient condition to generate indeterminacy and limit cycles in an endogenous growth model with public capital.

the indeterminacy of the equilibrium growth rate is not a mere mathematical curiosity but rather a relevant phenomenon that may occur in an economy with endogenous labor supply and public capital accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fiscal policy can be used as a tool to generate multiple growth patterns and to obtain global indeterminacy.
, even if the services derived from the public capital are congested by labor units, the dynamic equilibrium of the economy may still exhibit indeterminacy, local and global, and limit cycles.

the existence of public capital and its services, which are congested by households, may generate a richer and more complex dynamic equilibrium than those obtained in the standard neoclassical models of growth.
